evals.query: Here's the transcript from today's sign-off session on the team calendar app, plus some product context. What should we actually do with all this?
expected_behavior: Opens with 'What's being asked' in two or three sentences before any list
Sorts items into the five groups (Do now, Ask, Park, Not doing, Already handled), each with a short quote of the line that raised it
Puts public booking links under Not doing, citing the 2 September decision, even though the sales lead pushed for it twice
Puts the time-zone point under Already handled, pointing to release 1.4's time zone label and toggle

Surfaces the quiet empty-week line (new teams thinking it is broken) as Do now or Ask rather than dropping it, and prefers small changes (Today button, a changed-event marker) over the suggested week view redesign
Does not invent a figure the source did not give, such as an effort or cost for the admin console, and shows Do now as a table with the columns Change, Where, Why (the line) and Effort

evals.query: We ran five usability sessions on the recipe app yesterday. Here are my notes. What do we fix?
expected_behavior: Identifies the servings control not reading as a button as the real signal, quoting P2 and P4
Proposes a small change that clears the confusion (for example making the servings control look tappable) under Do now, rather than a redesign
Puts the video tutorial idea under Not doing, weighing P2's confusion as evidence but not their proposed solution
Puts the mood-board restyle (P3) under Not doing or Park with a one-line reason
Uses only counts the notes support (2 of 5 struggled with servings) and invents no percentages or extra participants
Ends by offering the Do now items as a sign-off page with getting-sign-off, and any open choice (such as asking for servings before Start cooking) as a question for settling-decisions

evals.query: This is the thread with the scale maker we're talking to for the fitness tracker. I have a call with her on Friday. What is she actually asking for, and what should we do?
expected_behavior: Decodes the ask in two or three sentences: she is setting conditions for a directory listing and asking what is realistic for the next release, not asking for everything to be built
Does not adopt the 'Lumen Sync' wording across the app, because nothing is signed and only changes true for any scale maker should be made now; puts it under Ask or Not doing with that reason
Treats the 24-month retention rule as the partner's own rule, weighs it as such, and flags the conflict with keeping history forever as an Ask item rather than deciding it
Puts 'a bit fragile' under Ask (which failures, how often) rather than inventing a cause, while noting the silent give-up after three retries as a provider-neutral fix
Parks body-composition support and says what it waits for (a signed agreement or a decision on new fields and a chart)
Uses the five-group structure with the line behind each item, and offers to draft the Friday reply with writing-briefs

trigger_checks.query: Here are my notes from the call with the plant care app's partner nursery. What are they really asking for?
The product lead left twenty comments on the notes app review doc. Which ones do we act on?
I pasted the transcript of this morning's usability round on the habit tracker. Turn it into what we fix, what we ask and what we drop.
Write a short reply to the head of support explaining why the shopping list order changed. She isn't technical.
We agreed to make the servings control look tappable. Show the team the current screen and the change side by side for approval.
We have twelve requests from customers and room for three this quarter. What goes first?
